key_insight: Fine-tuning RAFT on synthetic cavitating-flow images improves two-phase velocimetry, recovering near-wall reverse flow and flow rates consistent with independent measurements.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports flow diagnostics in cavitating hydraulic systems where vapor structures and optical distortion compromise conventional PIV.
method: Fine-tune RAFT on synthetic image pairs rendered from multiphase OpenFOAM simulations.
Compare RAFT-CloudCav with generalist RAFT, Farnebäck and OpenPIV on high-speed Venturi recordings.
Validate using metered flow rate, liquid-phase divergence and flow-rate consistency across stations.
evidence_signal: On 130,000-frame/s recordings, RAFT-CloudCav recovered 47.75 L/min versus a metered 48.0 ± 0.5 L/min, with 2.0% station-to-station variation versus 6–7% for classical methods.
watch_item: No experimental velocity ground truth is available, and coarse imaging severely under-resolves boundary-layer gradients even when bulk flow estimates appear accurate.
paper_title: Domain-Adapted Deep Optical Flow for Multiphase Velocimetry in Unsteady Cloud Cavitation
